{"final_output":{"message":"Hi Fatima,

Thanks so much for reaching out — it's great to hear you're interested in contributing to Jaseci ahead of GSoC! A few pointers to get you started:

**Repositories**
- Head over to our GitHub organization at github.com/Jaseci-Labs. The main repos to look at are:
  - **jaseci** — the core runtime and Jac compiler; a good place to start if you want to dig into the language and engine.
  - **jaseci-ai-kit** — Python-based AI/ML modules built on top of Jaseci; a great fit given your Python background.
  - **jaseci-serv** — the server/API layer if you're interested in backend and deployment.

**Good First Issues**
- In each repo, filter issues by the `good first issue` and `help wanted` labels. These are tagged specifically for newcomers and usually come with enough context to get going without deep prior knowledge of the codebase.

**Onboarding & Contribution Guidelines**
- Each repo has a `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the root — read it first for setup instructions, coding conventions, and PR workflow.
- The docs site (docs.jaseci.org) is also a good reference, and since you've already been learning Jac from there, you're ahead of the curve.

**Community Channels**
- Join our Discord (link in the repo READMEs or on jaseci.org) — that's where most day-to-day discussion happens, including GSoC Q&A and mentor office hours as the season approaches.
- Feel free to introduce yourself there and mention you're a prospective GSoC contributor; mentors and maintainers are happy to point you toward issues that align with your skills.

**A tip on timing**
- The earlier you start engaging — picking up small issues, asking questions on Discord, and submitting PRs — the stronger your GSoC application will be. Mentors love to see a track record of contributions before the application window opens, so don't wait!

If you have any trouble getting set up or finding an issue that fits, just reply here or ping us on Discord. Looking forward to seeing your first PR!

Best,
